text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). MagSafe is Apple's own branded version of the same idea. They're all magnetic and mostly cross-compatible. The main differences are speed and who certifies them.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Who** | WPC standard | WPC standard | Apple's brand and certification |
| **Max speed** | 15W | 25W | 15W, or 25W on newer chargers |
| **Magnets** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Works with** | iPhone 12/13 through 17, some Android with a magnetic case | iPhone 16 and later at full speed, plus a few Android phones | iPhone 12 and later |

**Qi2:** This added a magnetic ring to Qi so the phone and charger line up, which improves efficiency and speed. It was based on contributions from Apple's MagSafe tech ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). Speed is capped at 15W ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2:** Qi v2.2.1 is branded "Qi2 25W" and launched in July 2025. The WPC says it delivers nearly 70% more power, about 0 to 50% in roughly 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). Your phone has to support 25W too:
- Per [Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047), the iPhone 17 and 18 Pro series reach 25W, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach 22.5W, and the iPhone Air reaches 20W.
- The iPhone 17e tops out at 15W, and the 16e has no wireless charging ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).
- Among Android phones, the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports 25W. Other Pixel 10 models do 15W, and Samsung's Galaxy lineup is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**MagSafe:** This is Apple's certification program. Per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html), certified MagSafe chargers also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify the charger, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. In Macworld's tests, 15W MagSafe and 15W Qi2 charged at about the same speed. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W, so the two labels now overlap on Apple's own charger.

**Watch out for "MagSafe-compatible":** Macworld notes these uncertified chargers are usually 7.5W with a ring of magnets, so they take about twice as long to charge. They're often cheaper and fine if speed doesn't matter.

**What to buy:**
- **iPhone 16 or later:** Get a Qi2 25W-certified charger, like [Apple's MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8). The page I have shows the 2 m version at $49, and Macworld lists the 1 m at about $39. You'll need a 30W or higher USB-C adapter, sold separately, to hit 25W.
- **iPhone 15 or earlier:** A 15W Qi2 or MagSafe charger is all your phone can use. A 25W charger still works but won't be faster.
- **More options:** [Macworld's roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html) covers pads, stands, and multi-device chargers. For power banks, [The Verge's test](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks) picked the Baseus PicoGo AM52 as the fastest Qi2.2 battery.

You can confirm any charger's certification in the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
